explanation: Unlike in many Asian households, there's no national expectation to remove your shoes when entering a US home - it comes down to the individual host. Many Americans do ask guests to take shoes off, for cleanliness or to protect floors and carpets, especially in bad weather, but plenty of households don't mind either way.
local_tip: Look for a shoe pile or rack by the door, or simply ask your host, 'Should I take my shoes off?' when you arrive.

also_check.note: Removing shoes before entering a home is mandatory, with slippers typically provided for indoor use.
Very common to remove shoes indoors, especially in winter when floors and carpets need protecting from snow and salt.
In northeastern Brazil especially, guests are expected to remove their shoes before entering a home; keeping them on can be seen as rude.
